topic.readerProblem: A founder or marketer wants to know how to measure whether AI engines name their brand: which metrics to track, how to calculate them, how many prompts and repeats are enough, how often to re-measure, and how to tell a real change from run-to-run noise.
topic.connection: Measuring mentions, position, share of voice and citations across engines from unbranded buyer questions is exactly what AEOeye's audit does; the page explains the design behind that measurement, uses AEOeye's own benchmark as a denominator lesson, and says when a dedicated tracker fits better.

assessment: The page replaces an 18-term metrics dictionary and a statistics-roundup style guide with one checkable measurement design: four metrics plus an accuracy check with formulas, a minimum sampling design (30+ unbranded prompts, 3 to 5 runs, Wilson intervals with n set to the number of prompts), engine-by-engine test conditions taken from vendor documentation, a paired-prompt rule for calling a change real, and a build/buy/audit-once decision. It rests on vendor documentation checked on 3 October 2026, three 2026 arXiv preprints, the NIST handbook and AEOeye's own recommendation benchmark with its self-selection caveat. It deliberately does not quote third-party AI-visibility statistics, give a 'good score' target, compare engines from the benchmark, or claim anything about the ChatGPT or Claude apps beyond what the vendors document (it says apps can differ from APIs).

sources.supports: Single-author July 2026 preprint on 12,933 brand answers (3 models, 8 languages): one answer carries almost no brand-discriminating signal, repeats past the fifth barely help, spreading the budget across models or languages helps several times more.

Competitive set must be defined independently of model outputs because defining it from observed recommendations excludes brands LLMs rarely recommend (selection bias); recommendation is a stochastic process, not a single list.
Five LLMs configured to be deterministic still showed accuracy variations of up to 15% across 10 runs of the same tasks.
Anthropic Messages API reference: models released after Claude Opus 4.6 do not support setting temperature (only 1.0 accepted for backwards compatibility).
NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook 7.2.4.1 gives the Wilson method for confidence intervals for proportions and notes the common simple formula can produce a negative lower limit.
McNemar's test applies to paired dichotomous data and uses only discordant pairs; for few discordant pairs an exact binomial test with p = 0.5 on b + c is used.
Traffic from AI Overviews and AI Mode is included in Search Console's Web search type reporting; AI Overviews are only shown when Google's systems judge them additive and often do not trigger.
Google's help page for AI Overviews warns that AI responses can include mistakes.
AI Mode personalization references previous searches and activity saved in Search history when history and personalized recommendations are enabled.

OpenAI API web search tool: the model can choose whether to search; inline citations show only the most relevant references while a sources field lists every URL consulted; tool_choice required forces a search.

Claude determines when to search, searches for current information including about products and organizations, triggering is steerable through the system prompt, citations are always on, and an approximate user location can be set.
Gemini API grounding: the model analyzes the prompt and determines whether Google Search can improve the answer.
Gemini Apps can use saved info (personal context) and, gradually, past chats to shape responses, and users can switch personal context off or on.
Perplexity's migration page: Sonar Chat Completions support ended on 27 September 2026 and existing requests are being reformulated as Agent API requests, rolling out gradually by model.
Peec AI documentation: it runs prompts daily, and defines Visibility as how often the brand gets mentioned across AI responses.
Otterly homepage describes Share of AI Voice as the percentage of citations you own versus competitors.
